responses.prompt: Explain why the sky is blue, simply.
responses.response:
Sure! The sky appears blue because of something called Rayleigh scattering. Imagine you're looking at sunlight, which is made up of all the colors of the rainbow mixed together. When this light travels through Earth's atmosphere, it hits tiny particles in the air, like dust and water droplets.

The blue part of the light gets scattered more than other colors because blue light waves are shorter and bumpier as they travel through the air. This means that blue light scatters in all directions more easily than other colors. So, when you look up at the sky, you see all this scattered blue light bouncing back to your eyes from all around you, making the sky appear blue!

It's kind of like if you were playing with a flashlight and a big cloud of cotton balls. The flashlight light would scatter more in all directions when it hit the cotton balls, making the room brighter and more colorful. In the same way, the blue light scatters more in the atmosphere, making the sky look blue to us!
